title: Switching from trumpet to bass at the Gypsy Tea Room
summary: He played second trumpet at the Gypsy Tea Room, was asked to learn bass because players were scarce, and from about 1936 played with several bands before Kid Thomas.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Decatur Street. Uh, we used to wait practically all night. So, about eight till three in the morning, three or four o'clock in the morning. Uh, sometimes five o'clock. Me to play. And, uh, so after that, I got off trumpet. I started playing second trumpet with Rene at the Gypsy Tea Room. We opened up the Gypsy Tea Room. That was on, uh, St. Anne and Villaray. And bass players were scarce. And they had one of a bass players. So, they asked me, they said, Boyk, how about you, uh, trying to learn how to play bass? They said, bass players are scarce. I said, well, that'd be fine. I said, I'd like to play bass. So, I went and ran the bass from a kid. And, uh, Tillman, uh, I went and then Kimball. Kimball. Well, Kimball used to come through that night and Easter, show me the singing and different ideas on the bass, you know. Was the old man the played? No, the young, young man. The male character. The male character. So, I started playing bass then. I've been playing ever since. And I was around 1936. And then I started playing with all different bands. I played with Kit Howard a while. From Kit Howard, I played with Isaiah Morgan. And that's where I joined Kit Thomas band. I had been with him all the while. I played with him about 15, 16 years, Kit Thomas.
